profile.reading:
Iron Mountain Incorporated (NYSE: IRM) is a publicly traded REIT headquartered in Portsmouth, New Hampshire. The company has two distinct lines of business relevant here: a decades-old, much larger physical and digital records-management segment operated out of a large number of warehouse-type facilities nationally, and a newer data center REIT segment built substantially through a January 2018 acquisition of IO Data Centers, spanning more than 30 marketed locations globally.

This address, 2859 South 18th Place in Phoenix, Arizona, is tagged in source mapping data as a data center, but Iron Mountain's own data center site names exactly four active Phoenix-area IT facilities for this metro: AZP-1, AZP-2, AZP-3, and the separate Scottsdale campus AZS-1, none of which correspond to this South 18th Place address. That address instead sits in an industrial corridor south of Phoenix Sky Harbor airport, a location and naming pattern ("Records Storage") consistent with Iron Mountain's much larger core records-management business rather than its marketed colocation data center portfolio.

This registry records that inference honestly rather than asserting data center specifications that have not been found: no IT capacity, technical or building square footage, year opened, or tier certification for this specific address was located in operator or public sourcing this session, and none is asserted. Readers researching Iron Mountain's actual Phoenix-area data center capacity should look to the AZP-1, AZP-2, and AZP-3 buildings on Iron Mountain's roughly 39-acre Phoenix campus, plus the separate AZS-1 Scottsdale campus, all tracked elsewhere in this registry, rather than to this address. Confirming this facility's exact function (records storage versus some other use) would require direct verification with Iron Mountain or a Maricopa County Assessor parcel lookup, neither of which this registry has completed.

reading.body:
This facility does not appear in Iron Mountain's marketed data center portfolio. Iron Mountain operates four separate Phoenix-area IT campuses under the AZP and AZS designations on its own data center location pages, none at this South 18th Place address in central Phoenix. The address instead sits in an industrial corridor consistent with Iron Mountain's core records-management business line, which operates separate warehouse facilities across the country for physical and digital records storage, imaging, and destruction services.

No IT capacity, building specifications, or tier certification have been published for this address. Iron Mountain's own data center pages do not list it, and no sourcing in the public record associates megawatts, square footage, or infrastructure credentials with 2859 South 18th Place. This facility appears to be a miscategorization in mapping data rather than a data center campus.

This address should not be used to assess Iron Mountain's actual Phoenix-area data center capacity. Readers evaluating the company's colocation footprint in the state should instead reference the AZP-1, AZP-2, and AZP-3 campuses on Iron Mountain's published Phoenix page, plus AZS-1 in Scottsdale. Arizona has four data center facilities with published megawatt figures totaling 512 MW across the state.
